newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Independent makes slow progress on W&H bid.
newsitem.headline: Independent makes slow progress on W&H bid.

text.p: Independent Press Communications, a unit of Independent Newspapers Plc, made slow progress on Thursday on the first day of its stand in the market for Wilson & Horton Ltd shares,.
Independent's broker BZW said it picked up just 60,000 shares in morning trade in its $11.00 per share bid for the New Zealand newspaper publisher.
W&H shares rose one cent to $11.01 against a weak market.
There was turnover of 459,725 shares, most of which went to other brokers which were picking up the shares to exchange for Independent shares.

Independent is attempting to buy the 54 million shares, 55 percent, it does not already control. It has a two-pronged offer -- a written offer which opened on Thursday and will remain open until at least November 8, and a stand in the market for cash at $11.00 per share which also opened today through BZW.
The written offer is for cash or to exchange 1.375 Independent shares for one W&H share up to a limit of 40 million Independent shares. The exchangeable offer is on a first-come-first-served basis.
Analysts believe the exchange offer values W&H at considerably above the $11.00 cash price -- between $11.50-$12.00 -- and they are taking arbitrage opportunities.
"We view it as a good start," said BZW Managing Director Simon Allen of today's activity.
He said there had been a high level of interest in the exchangable share part of the offer because of its perceived higher value.

Allen said in general investors would be waiting until after the outcome of Saturday's general election to assess the value of the offer. "We expect significant acceptances to come in over the next week," he said.
